Vendor Stability.content: Dust was founded in 2022 by former Stripe engineers Gabriel Hubert and Stanislas Polu, with Polu also having spent three years at OpenAI (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/). The company has raised over $60 million in total funding (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/), including a $40 million Series B round led by Sequoia and Abstract, with Datadog and Snowflake joining as new investors (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/). Following the Series B, Dust announced plans to double headcount across engineering and go-to-market teams by year-end (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/). No layoffs, leadership departures, shutdown rumors, or signs of financial distress or acquisition were found in the search results. The company claims zero churn since the beginning of 2025, with over 3,000 client organizations and more than 300,000 agents deployed, achieving a 70% weekly active usage rate (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/).
Vendor Stability.source_type: self-reported, corroborated by named press sources

Incident History.content: A vulnerability was identified on GitHub (Issue #4556) concerning unauthorized use of external image hosting, where an attacker could intercept assistant creation requests and modify the "pictureUrl" field to include an image hosted on a different server or a link to a large file, potentially leading to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks (https://github.com/dust-tt/dust/issues/4556). No data breaches, major outages, or lawsuits related to data handling or security beyond this single vulnerability were found in the search results.

Community Signal.content: On G2, users praise Dust's user-friendliness, fast rollout, and high daily active usage in deployments (https://www.g2.com/products/dust-tt/reviews). Common complaints include that setup takes time, requires a good knowledge base, and is considered expensive at $29/user/month for the Pro plan (https://www.g2.com/products/dust-tt/reviews). G2 reviewers also highlight responsive support and an active Slack community, though documentation gaps for advanced features are a recurring criticism (https://www.g2.com/products/dust-tt/reviews). No specific Reddit, Hacker News, or Twitter/X sentiment was found in the search results.
Community Signal.source_type: named platform (G2), small sample size noted

Compliance Posture.content:
- SOC 2 Type II: Dust claims this certification on its enterprise page and it is also mentioned in third-party reviews such as Cybernews and a French article (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/) (https://www.journaldunet.com/intelligence-artificielle/1539772-dust-ai-leve-36-millions-de-dollars-pour-sa-plateforme-d-agents-ia/) (though no named auditor is provided).
- GDPR: Dust states compliance on its enterprise page and this is echoed in third-party sources (https://www.journaldunet.com/intelligence-artificielle/1539772-dust-ai-leve-36-millions-de-dollars-pour-sa-plateforme-d-agents-ia/).
- HIPAA: Dust claims on its enterprise page that it "enables HIPAA compliance," and this is also mentioned in the Cybernews review (https://www.cybernews.com/news/dust-ai-safe-to-use/).
- ISO 27001: Listed by a third-party comparison site (Volvenix) (https://volvenix.com/en/tools/compare/dust-tt-vs-ainize-ai-3/), but no vendor confirmation or auditor details were found.
- PCI DSS and FedRAMP: No information found.
Compliance Posture.source_type: self-reported (source explicitly notes "no named auditor is provided" for SOC2 claim)

Data Handling Posture.content: Customer data is stored on Google Cloud Platform (in the USA or EU), with database provider Qdrant Solutions GmbH used for storing data embeddings (https://www.dust.tt/legal/security). Hosting region can be selected at workspace creation for Enterprise customers (https://www.dust.tt/legal/security). Dust and foundation model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Google, Fireworks.ai) are prohibited from using Customer Data for model training (https://www.dust.tt/legal/security). Foundation Model Providers apply a "Zero Data Retention" policy, meaning Customer Content will not be logged for human review and will not be saved to disk or retained by those providers (https://www.dust.tt/legal/security). A full list of subprocessors and third parties is available in Dust's Sub-Processors Notice, including infrastructure providers (Google Cloud Platform, Qdrant, SendGrid, Datadog, E2B, Cloudflare), foundation model providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, Google, Fireworks.ai, ElevenLabs), and operations providers (Customer.io, Front, Hubspot, Snowflake, Stripe, PostHog, Novu) (https://www.dust.tt/legal/subprocessors). No specific retention policy details were found beyond the zero retention policy for foundation model providers.

Integration Risk.content: Dust offers a RESTful API for custom integrations, Webhook support for event-driven workflows, MCP (Model Context Protocol) for proprietary systems, OAuth2 for third-party app permissions, bi-directional sync (read + write actions), and incremental data refresh (https://www.dust.tt/developers/docs). The platform provides over 100 connectors to data sources and business software (https://www.dust.tt/connectors). Dust positions itself as having no vendor lock-in, allowing users to switch between best-in-class models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral) without rewriting logic and to redeploy agents to different models (https://www.dust.tt/developers/docs). A technical user can export data using the Open API (https://www.dust.tt/developers/docs). However, some comparison sites note "no public API available" (https://volvenix.com/en/tools/compare/dust-tt-vs-ainize-ai-3/), and advanced governance controls may be enterprise-only. Overall lock-in risk appears low due to model flexibility and Open API access, though complex workflows may create operational dependency.
